fixedRejects: glassmorphism / glow / lens-flare / gradient-drenched AI-SaaS looks
acceptFrame: dark, warm, restrained, instrument-grade dashboard / settings / config-panel / developer-tool / console UIs; judge HIERARCHY / LAYOUT / DENSITY / TYPOGRAPHY / RESTRAINT, not palette.
acceptNuance: Single-accent discipline: accept reference UIs where the accent color is NOT amber but is used with the same semantic restraint — one warm-tone accent (ochre, brass, gold, burnt orange) applied only to active state, CTA, and sequence markers, never as background fill or decoration

Grid substrate signal: accept references that show a very faint engineering grid or micro-texture as a page background even if barely visible — this substrate is a load-bearing impeccable cue indicating instrument-grade intent, not minimalism

Three-family typographic jurisdiction: prioritize references that visibly commit three font families to three distinct roles (display for headlines, humanist sans for body, mono for code/labels/status) with NO overlap — the family is the role

Hairline-only separation: accept references that divide sections exclusively with 1px rules and opacity shifts — no filled dividers, no section backgrounds, no shadow-based z-separation; the layout is flat and the rules do the work

Near-zero radius: treat 2px radius as the aesthetic ceiling — any reference using pill-shaped components, large rounded cards (>8px), or capsule-heavy layouts should be REJECTED even if the palette is otherwise correct

Accept a fine engineering-grid substrate (40–50px repeating line grid in a near-invisible tone) as intentional texture — it reads as instrument-grade, not decorative noise; pieces with this pattern score above flat-dark equivalents
Accept amber-singleton design systems where amber is provably the only accent across the entire UI — multi-accent dark UIs (teal + amber + purple status dots) score lower even if otherwise restrained

Accept typographic brand lockups that mix two or three font families in a single horizontal compound — this is the structural pattern here, and hunting only single-family brands will miss the right reference class

Accept toggle switches and interactive controls where STATE is carried by position/shape first, color second — the knob-position-primary pattern is an accessibility and instrument-grade signal worth filtering for

Prefer pieces where the terminal/preview chrome is minimal-literal: three dots are present but not colorful traffic-lights; the chrome is identifiable as terminal but does not cosplay macOS — restrained signification over fidelity

Accept zero-padded sequence markers (01 02 03) as functional step indicators when they are small and typographically subordinate to the step title — reject pieces where large numerals are the hero visual of the section

Accept UIs where a faint 1px engineering substrate grid (~46px repeat) is visible through the page background as a deliberate textural signal of instrument-grade design — this is not a layout grid artifact and should be weighted positively

Accept step-head patterns where the number is typographically raw with no container shape — the absence of a circle or badge around '01' is the specific restraint marker; reject any reference wrapping step numbers in colored chips, filled circles, or outlined pills

Accept terminal preview titlebar dots that are deliberately asymmetric: 2 empty hairline circles + 1 amber-filled circle — this asymmetry is the design intent, not an incomplete mockup; reject references with uniformly colored dot rows or rainbow traffic lights
Accept near-zero radius throughout (≤3px) as an instrument-sharpness signal — the rejection threshold for rounded-card aesthetic is ≥8px; 2px radius reads as sharp, purposeful, and operator-grade

Accept brand mastheads where amber appears in at most 2 specific typographic nodes out of the full lockup — amber as area fill or background wash for the masthead band is a rejection signal even on otherwise dark UIs

Typography carries hierarchy even without color: mono badges for code/IDs, Big-Shoulders-class display-weight uppercase for headings, regular-weight body — an example with no amber visible but correct typographic discipline should still score high

The 46px engineering crosshatch grid at hairline opacity is a signature substrate — accept any dark UI using grid, graph-paper, or dot-matrix background texture even if the grid color differs, because the pattern signals instrument-grade rather than consumer
Border-radius is a hard filter at 2px: reject any panel, card, or container with radius ≥8px — it immediately reads consumer app, not operator console, regardless of palette

Single-accent monovalence is a quality gate: if a UI uses more than one hue as a positive signal color it breaks Almanac Noir discipline — only amber-family accent plus one ember/alert hue reserved for destructive states is acceptable

The 5% amber-opacity header gradient fading to transparent over 80% is acceptable and desirable on the masthead — it is NOT the glassmorphism rejection criterion, which targets full-saturation multi-stop gradients and glow blooms

brand: Seek: horizontal strip where a monospace badge (short product code, contained in a thin-bordered capsule) is set inline beside a heavier display-weight wordmark — the mark and the name use different font families with different size and weight by structural jurisdiction, not decoration

Look for: sub-label (version, category, or descriptor) in a third family (small-caps or spaced mono) at a much smaller size, aligned to center or baseline of the strip — functioning as a semantic tier, not an afterthought
Pattern to find: the whole lockup reads as instrument-panel nameplate, not a logo — it is part of the chrome, subordinate to the app, never centered or hero-sized
REJECT if: the brand is isolated, oversized, animated, uses a custom logomark glyph, or fills more than ~30% of the header strip width

Sticky header band where brand is PURELY typographic: a monospace chip/badge (short code, border-outlined, no icon) + condensed uppercase display wordmark + small monospace sub-label — all baseline-aligned in one horizontal group; reject patterns where an icon or glyph leads
Mixed font-family lockup: mono for the badge/chip, a condensed or wide-display family for the primary name, mono for the sub-label — the typographic contrast IS the brand identity
Amber (or equivalent single warm accent) used only on the chip/badge and the accent syllable of the wordmark — not as a background fill on the whole header
Background treatment: panel-tone header separated from page ground by a single hairline rule, possibly a very faint vertical gradient toward transparent — not a thick colored bar or drop shadow

Hunt for a sticky header band containing a compact inline typographic lockup with 3 horizontal tiers in one flex row: (1) a boxed micro-prefix in monospace+amber with hairline border, (2) a display-weight uppercase wordmark with amber highlight on one syllable only, (3) a spaced mono sub-label at a smaller size — all baseline-aligned, NOT stacked vertically and NOT centered on the page

Structural tell: the badge uses a hairline border + slightly elevated panel background making it a distinct chromatic node without being decorative; the amber partial on tier 2 echoes the badge color without doubling it; both amber hits together are ≤2 nodes in the full lockup
Reject: centered hero branding, full-width brand color bands, logos with padding zones, any treatment where brand floats outside header flow or amber fills the entire masthead background

Hunt for masthead lockups pairing a small monospaced badge/chip (hairline border, elevated bg, 2–3px letter-spacing) with a large display-weight uppercase wordmark — the badge is a code-style abbrev anchoring identity, the wordmark carries the product name
Look for the three-tier horizontal composition at baseline alignment: [mono code chip] [display-font product name] [allcaps mono subtitle in secondary tone] — horizontal flow, NOT stacked rows
Prefer headers where the accent appears on exactly one element in the brand cluster (the chip fill or a single word/letter), leaving the rest in warm neutrals — accent scarcity is the quality signal

Sticky top-bar: brand cluster left, action buttons right, hairline bottom rule, bar tone slightly elevated from page ground — no heavy drop shadow, no full-bleed gradient, at most a faint 5% amber wash fading 80% down
step-heads: Seek: large tabular numerals in a monospace or condensed face, amber or accent-tinted, sitting to the left of a two-tier text block (title line + descriptor line) — the number is typographic, NOT enclosed in a bubble, circle, or pill
Pattern: number and title share a BASELINE alignment (not center or top), so the number reads as a column marker in a tight prose grid rather than a milestone badge

Look for: the descriptor line constrained to ~60–70ch, rendered in a secondary weight/color, clearly subordinate — the step-head has three distinct optical weights in three lines: accent numeral → display uppercase title → body-weight description
REJECT if: the number sits inside a circle/badge, if connector lines link the steps (stepper/wizard pattern), or if all three tiers are the same color/weight
Number is a small (12–15px) fixed-width prefix in monospace accent color, zero-padded (01/02/03), baseline-aligned with the h2 — NOT a large decorative numeral floated left or centered above
h2 in a condensed or wide-display family, uppercase, weight 600–700, ~22–28px, immediately adjacent to the number with a tight gap (~12–16px)
One-line description in a body-weight sans at ~13–14px in a subdued secondary tone, sitting 6–10px below the h2 — not a full paragraph, not bold

The entire step-head is flush-left with no enclosing card or box; the body panel (step-body) is a separate bordered block below it; hierarchy is achieved through typography alone, not spatial containers around the head

Hunt for a baseline-aligned flex row of [number marker] + [div with title+desc] where the number is a raw monospace amber '0N' label — no circle, no pill, no icon, no background fill, no stroke ring — and the title uses a condensed/display face at ~25px uppercase, with the desc in smaller body weight below

The CSS ::before prepends '0' to make '1'→'01' purely via content property; hunt for references that treat step numbers as typographic counters rather than progress-indicator shapes — the number's function is section-label, not stepper-stage

Structural tell: the step-body is a hairline-bordered panel-bg rectangle that follows immediately below the step-head with a gap — this makes the number+title a section divider, not a wizard-flow stage; reject any numbered-steps reference that implies linearity with connectors or progress fills

Hunt for numbered section dividers where the numeral is typographically isolated: mono or display-font, accent-colored, zero-padded (01/02/03), sitting at baseline with the section title — NOT boxed, NOT inside a circle, just inline flow

The structural triad: [accent numeral] + [display-font uppercase heading at line-height ≤1] + [subdued single-line descriptor at 13–14px in secondary tone] — total block height under 56px, tight vertical rhythm
Numeral must read as a semantic sequence marker not hero art — reject examples where numbers are oversized decorative elements with no hierarchical relationship to the heading
Prefer examples where the numeral and heading share a flex baseline-align row with a fixed 12–16px gap, so the number optically registers as a prefix rather than a separate element
terminal-preview: Seek: a framed terminal or code window that is EMBEDDED inside a larger application layout — the frame is part of the configurator UI, not a hero illustration or standalone mockup

The titlebar chrome must be minimal and functional: a left-anchored dot group (3 circles, simple, non-skeuomorphic), a centered title in spaced mono uppercase, and a RIGHT-SIDE interactive control (slider, column picker, or similar) — all three zones present in a single compact bar
Look for: the preview content area rendered DARKER than its frame (ground darker than panel), creating a recessed-instrument reading: the frame housing is warmer/lighter, the output well is deeper
The frame border should be a hairline (1px) — the window reads as an incision in the layout, not a card floating above it — 2px radius or less

REJECT if: the frame is a realistic macOS/Windows chrome illustration, if it uses drop-shadow or glow to lift it, if the dots use actual traffic-light red/yellow/green fills, or if the terminal is used as a decorative hero element

Chrome bar with three distinct regions: traffic-light dots (left) / centered monospace uppercase title / inline control (right, e.g. a range slider with a cols-badge) — all in a single bar, NOT split across two rows

Traffic-light dots that are partially hollow — at least one or two rendered as border-only circles with transparent fill; the active/filled dot in an accent color rather than the conventional green; this signals 'restrained, non-literal' chrome
Preview body set on a darker background than the chrome bar and surrounding panel (ground-dark under the chrome's panel-hi), creating a recessed well effect with the content appearing inset
Range slider for viewport/column width control sitting inline in the chrome bar itself (not below the preview), with accent-colored thumb/track and a small monospace badge showing the live value
Bottom footnote in monospace at ~11px in a subdued tone, separated by a hairline — 'Approximate' or equivalent disclaimer; confirms this is a live-render element, not a static mockup

Hunt for a terminal window frame embedded mid-page (between sticky header and form sections) with: (a) a titlebar containing traffic-light dots where only one dot has fill (amber/accent) and the other two are empty hairline circles; (b) a centered uppercase mono title in the titlebar; (c) a range slider right-aligned in the titlebar for column-width with an amber-accented badge readout; (d) a content area on a background DARKER than the outer container

Structural tell: the window carries an inset box-shadow at ~6% amber opacity — a barely-there amber inset glow at the interior edge, not an outer glow ring; this is the restraint signal to hunt for specifically

Accept titlebar layouts where the col-width badge is a mono amber label in a hairline box flush with the slider — this control is structurally part of the titlebar chrome, not a caption below the window; reject terminal frames where the width control is external to the titlebar band

Hunt for terminal/shell output frames with a minimal titlebar containing: simplified traffic-light dots (flattened, muted, or only one active), a centered monospaced allcaps title, and an inline range slider with a value badge/readout showing the current setting

The two-tone structural split is the key pattern: titlebar at elevated panel tone + output area at a darker ground tone, both inside a single hairline-bordered outer frame with 2px radius — no rounded pill frame, no thick bezel

The column-width slider + readout badge pair is the distinguishing control — look for range inputs inline with a small token displaying the live value (e.g. '200 cols') in mono font with a hairline border
Accept frames with a faint footnote/disclaimer line at the bottom in mono secondary-tone type — this 'approximate rendering' footer is a live-preview configurator signature
